solution.brief: Sets up a Wasp stochastic aggregation system with two distinct basic parts defined by Brep geometry and directional connections, governed by text-based assembly rules to generate rule-driven discrete spatial aggregations.
solution.principle:
Related insight: Related insight: While this pattern uses Brep geometry with direction-curve-based connections, Wasp also supports mesh-based parts where connections are derived directly from mesh vertices and edges — bypassing the need for explicit direction curves. This mesh-vertex/edge connection approach is an alternative to Wasp_Connection From Direction and is demonstrated in tutorial 03.

Related insight: Related insight: Tutorial 04 extends this two-part Brep aggregation setup by adding Weaverbird Catmull-Clark subdivision smoothing as a post-processing step. The aggregation logic remains identical; the difference is that the extracted part geometry is subsequently smoothed using Weaverbird, enabling a smooth mesh preview of the discrete assembly in addition to the raw Brep output.

Related insight: Related insight: Tutorial 05 presents the same two-part Brep aggregation setup (directional connections, text-based rules, stochastic aggregation) without any Weaverbird post-processing. This confirms that the core two-part workflow is self-contained and complete without mesh subdivision — Weaverbird is an optional visualization enhancement, not a required step. Tutorial 05 serves as the minimal clean reference for two-part discrete aggregation.

Related insight: Related insight: Tutorial 06 extends the two-part stochastic aggregation workflow (established in tutorials 02–05) by adding custom attributes to part definitions and exporting aggregation results via a file update component. This establishes file-based export as a third post-processing pathway alongside Weaverbird mesh smoothing (tutorial 04) and plain visualization (tutorial 05).

Related insight: Related insight: Tutorial 02 (this pattern) extends the foundational single-part workflow from tutorial 01 (wasp_01_basic_aggregation) by introducing a second distinct part type. Tutorial 01 is the prerequisite: it establishes the core 5-step pattern (geometry → connections → WaspPart → Rules → Stochastic Aggregation) with a single part before the two-part rule complexity introduced here. Learners should complete tutorial 01 before attempting this two-part setup.

Related insight: Related insight: The wasp_02_rule_grammar pattern explicitly focuses on the rule grammar layer of this tutorial series — specifically, how multiple rules encode directionality to control which connections can mate and in what orientation. This two-part setup (tutorial 02) is closely related: the rule grammar knowledge underpins the text-based rule strings used here, and understanding connection-mating directionality is essential for correctly specifying the cross-part rule set.

Related insight: Related insight: Tutorial 03 (wasp_03_graph_grammar) introduces graph grammar as an alternative aggregation strategy to the stochastic approach used in this tutorial. Rather than random part placement guided by rules, graph grammar constrains aggregation to follow a predefined graph structure — enabling designed, reproducible connectivity topologies. The two-part rule setup established here is a stepping stone toward understanding how graph grammar extends rule-based control over assembly.

Related insight: Related insight: Field-driven aggregation (wasp_04_field_driven) represents an advanced extension of the two-part stochastic setup established in this tutorial. By introducing scalar fields (attractors or density gradients), the aggregation engine biases part selection and placement — the same two-part rule vocabulary is retained, but growth is steered spatially by field values rather than being uniformly random. This is a complementary pathway to Weaverbird smoothing (tutorial 04) and file export (tutorial 06).

intents: create a stochastic aggregation with wasp
generate modular aggregation with connection rules

evolution_history.changes: New pattern reveals an alternative connection-derivation method (mesh vertices/edges) that complements the Brep+direction-curve approach used here, expanding the known connection definition strategies.

wasp_basic_aggregation_02 is the direct predecessor to tutorial 04 — same two-part Brep setup. Users of pattern 02 should know that tutorial 04 demonstrates how to add Weaverbird smoothing as a visualization enhancement to this exact setup.

Tutorial 05 is the direct sibling of tutorial 02 — same two-part Brep aggregation but without Weaverbird. Adding this context clarifies the relationship between the tutorials and confirms the workflow's self-sufficiency without post-processing.
Tutorial 02 has extensive context on the tutorial series progression; it should note that tutorial 06 adds attributes and file export as further extensions.

Tutorial 02 builds directly on tutorial 01 but had no explicit reference to that prerequisite. The new pattern's addition clarifies the tutorial sequence. Adding beginner/prerequisite tags and a lineage context note helps learners navigate from tutorial 01 to tutorial 02 in the correct order.

wasp_basic_aggregation_02 and wasp_02_rule_grammar are both tutorial-02-level content; the new pattern's focus on rule grammar and connection-mating directionality directly enriches the rule-definition step of this two-part aggregation pattern.

The two-part stochastic aggregation pattern (tutorial 02) is a direct predecessor to the graph grammar tutorial. Adding context about graph grammar helps learners understand the progression from stochastic to structured aggregation.
The two-part aggregation tutorial should document the field-driven pathway as an advanced extension alongside the other post-processing and extension tutorials it already references.
